text.title: Mistake Memory Core Rules
text.summary: 17 testable rules every Mistake Memory application must enforce: capture timing and triggers, entry fields, error-category tags, and the four prevention layers. These are HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

section.title: Background
section.p: Rules r-capture-within-24h through r-third-recurrence-ci-rule are the capture rules: when to capture a mistake, minimum required fields, and quality standards for entries. Rules r-tag-hallucination-api through r-tag-instruction-drift, with the lists below, are the taxonomy of LLM agent failure modes used to classify MIS-NNN entries and select prevention strategies. Rules r-pre-task-warning-injection through r-multi-model-review-high-severity are the four-layer defense against recurring mistakes: pre-task warnings, quality gates, CI automation, and multi-model review.

list.item: missing-error-handling: try/catch absent in async flows, silent failures in payment or critical paths
edge-cases-missed: boundary conditions, empty arrays, null fields not handled
scope-creep: unrequested features added during implementation
premature-optimization: performance changes before correctness verified
skipped-validation: quality gate bypassed, pre-commit hook skipped
estimation-underrun: task took 2x+ estimated tokens due to unknown unknowns
missing-env-var: new config variable not propagated to all environments
data-migration-no-backup: destructive operation without prior backup

section.reference: MIS-NNN entry template with all required fields
Bash script for keyword-based warning injection

rule.statement: Mistake MUST be written within 30 min of detection; later writeback rejected.
rule.rationale: Memory written hours later is reconstructive. The two sources disagree on the capture window: this rule and the procedure say 30 minutes, while r-capture-within-24h allows 24 hours; this rule governs until reconciled.

rule.statement: Root-cause chain MUST be ≥3 levels of Why; shallower analysis rejected.
Prevention step MUST be concrete ("add lint rule X", "add CI check Y"); generic preventions ("be careful") rejected.
rule.rationale: Generic preventions are wishes, not rules.

rule.statement: Relevant mistakes MUST be injected into agent context before similar tasks.
Second occurrence of the same mistake MUST trigger an automatic CI rule.
rule.rationale: Second occurrence is the signal that human discipline failed. The two sources disagree on the occurrence count: this rule, the procedure and r-recurrence-ci-rule say the second occurrence, while r-third-recurrence-ci-rule says the third; this rule governs until reconciled.

rule.statement: Document a mistake within 24 hours of the failure. Do not defer — details fade within a single conversation turn.
rule.rationale: Incomplete entries written days later omit root cause and specific context, making them useless for future warning injection.

rule.statement: Capture when: a bug reaches production, CI fails unexpectedly, the same error occurs twice, a task takes more than 2x estimated tokens, or an agent hallucinates an API or feature.
rule.rationale: These signals identify pattern-level failures worth documenting. One-off typos do not require entries.

rule.statement: Every MIS-NNN entry must include: severity (critical/high/medium/low), what happened (specific description), root cause (Five Whys chain, minimum 3 levels), and one concrete prevention step.
rule.rationale: Entries without root cause cannot generate useful prevention rules. Entries without prevention are read-only history, not actionable warnings.

rule.statement: When a pattern recurs a third time, add an automated CI prevention rule; documenting the same entry twice is not sufficient.
rule.rationale: Documentation is awareness, not enforcement. Recurring patterns require automated blocking to actually prevent recurrence.

rule.statement: Tag entries with `hallucination-api` when the agent invents a non-existent library method or endpoint. Prevention: include API reference documentation in task context.
rule.rationale: LLMs pattern-match from similar APIs and generate syntactically plausible but non-existent calls with full confidence. Type checking and tests are the only reliable catches.

rule.statement: Tag entries with `hallucination-factual` when the agent confidently states a new feature, version, or behavior that does not exist. Prevention: ask for documentation links; treat any unverified "new in X" claim as unverified.
rule.rationale: The 64.5% blind-spot rate in self-correction studies means the agent cannot reliably flag its own factual errors. External verification is required.

rule.statement: Tag entries with `context-window-loss` when earlier instructions drift out of the effective context. Prevention: break tasks exceeding 300 lines into chunks; include a coding standards summary with each chunk.
rule.rationale: Models become unreliable at 65-80% of advertised context limits. Long conversations cause instruction drift even within the stated window.

rule.statement: Tag entries with `instruction-drift` when requirements specified at session start are not honored mid-task. Prevention: re-inject key constraints every N tool calls or task boundaries.
rule.rationale: Instruction drift is distinct from window loss — the instruction is technically in context but deprioritized by later content.

rule.statement: Before executing any task, keyword-search mistakes.md and prepend matching entries as a Warnings section in the task prompt.
rule.rationale: Agents that skip pre-task loading get no benefit from the accumulated mistake corpus. Injection must be explicit and automated, not optional.

rule.statement: SDD quality gates L1-L6 are the structural enforcement of lessons from past mistakes. Each gate failure generates a mistake entry.
rule.rationale: Gates create mandatory checkpoints that block progression when known failure conditions are detected, replacing optional checklists.

rule.statement: When a mistake pattern recurs, add an automated CI rule using a file pattern, keyword trigger, or code pattern detector.
rule.rationale: Documentation without enforcement is only awareness. Patterns that survive two documented occurrences require code-level blocking.

rule.statement: For high-severity mistakes (critical/high), add a cross-validation step where a second agent or model reviews the primary output.
rule.rationale: Self-evaluation has a 64.5% blind-spot rate. A second independent pass catches logical inconsistencies the first model cannot see in its own output.
